title: Rebuilding a tooth with a post
what: If little of the tooth is left, a post or a core is placed in the root. A filling or crown is then attached to it.
why: After a root canal, when the top of the tooth is badly broken down.
duration: usually 1 to 2 visits of 30 to 60 minutes
tell_doctor: If the tooth was treated before, and when
If the tooth hurts when you bite
If you are allergic to numbing medicine or dental materials

prepare.title: X-ray
prepare.text: A recent X-ray of the tooth is usually needed. It will be taken at the clinic.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Eat beforehand. Your mouth will be numb for a while after the visit.

prepare.title: Root canals
prepare.text: Before a post, the root canals must be well filled. The doctor will check this.

steps: The doctor checks the tooth and the X-ray
If needed, you get numbing medicine
Part of the canal filling is removed
A ready-made post is placed, or an impression is taken for a custom core
The post is fixed with special cement
The tooth is rebuilt with a filling or prepared for a crown
feel: It usually does not hurt. You may feel vibration from the tools
You may feel pressure when the post is placed
after: Do not eat until the numbness wears off
Avoid hard food on that tooth until the crown is on
A custom core usually takes a few days to make
The crown is placed as your doctor plans
red_flags: Severe pain when biting that lasts several days
Swelling of the gum near the tooth
The post or temporary filling fell out

faq.q: Do I always need a crown on a tooth with a post?
faq.a: Often, yes. It lowers the risk of the tooth cracking. Your doctor decides.

faq.q: How long does a post last?
faq.a: Usually many years, if the tooth has a crown and you protect it from hard food.

reminders.text: Tooth rebuilding tomorrow. Eat beforehand and bring past X-rays.
